text:
For a relativistic particle the total energy is  

E = γ mc² , where γ = 1/√(1–β²) and β = v/c.

1. Speed  
   β = 0.96 ⇒ γ = 1 / √(1 – 0.96²)  
                  = 1 / √(1 – 0.9216)  
                  = 1 / √0.0784  
                  = 1 / 0.28  
                  = 3.571428…

2. Rest-mass energy of the Li-6 nucleus  
   A Li-6 nucleus has 3 protons + 3 neutrons.  
   Taking the averaged nucleon rest-mass energy mₙ ≃ 0.9315 GeV, the nuclear rest energy is  

   m c² ≈ 6 × 0.9315 GeV ≃ 5.589 GeV.

   (Using the known atomic mass of 6.015 u and removing the electron masses gives 5.602 GeV; either value differs by only ≈0.2%.)

   We will use the more accurate 5.60 GeV.

3. Total energy at β = 0.96  
   E = γ mc² ≃ 3.571428 × 5.60 GeV ≃ 20.0 GeV.

Among the given choices the value closest to this is 20.132 GeV.

Answer: A
